use.chart/timeseries: Compare timestamped measurements over the same interval. Supply labeled series with explicit units; the shared axes make changes in API and worker throughput directly comparable.
use.input/text: Collect a single editable value such as an environment name. Use a labeled field when the value also needs persistent help or validation feedback.
use.pattern/log-inspector: Investigate one HTTP exchange alongside its correlated application logs. Request and response payloads keep separate viewports while the parent coordinates selection, focus and available space.
use.collection/files: Let someone browse a directory and select an allowed file type. Initialize the native picker before capturing its view so the example contains actual files.
use.foundations/focus: Route keyboard input among nested regions while keeping only the active child focused. The parent owns navigation between regions and forwards child commands.
use.foundations/layout: Allocate terminal-cell rectangles before rendering a composition. Panels reserve borders and gutters so child components receive the space they can actually use.
use.chart/sparkline: Show a compact numeric trend beside a current value or inside a table cell. Use a full time-series chart when readers need labeled axes and timestamps.
use.chart/line: Plot numeric observations on explicit horizontal and vertical axes. Choose this primitive when you need direct control over the native line renderer and its data range.
use.chart/scatter: Compare the position of individual observations on two numeric axes. Use distinct markers and labels when multiple groups need to remain recognizable without color.
use.chart/bars: Compare category magnitudes in a fixed terminal allocation. Supply meaningful labels and a consistent scale so the lengths represent comparable quantities.
use.chart/heatmap: Show ordered intensity across a grid of observations. The sequential palette encodes magnitude independently of category identity; include numeric context when exact values matter.
use.chart/stream: Show the most recent numeric samples as a scrolling trace. Use this for a live trend whose recent shape matters more than a complete historical time axis.
use.chart/wave: Draw a waveform over a numeric range with native line geometry. Supply the observed points explicitly and keep the range stable when comparing successive frames.
use.chart/ohlc: Compare open, high, low and close observations over an ordered series. The native candle renderer preserves the supplied measurements; the application owns their units and interpretation.
use.chart/canvas: Place styled text and individual marks at exact terminal-cell coordinates. Use higher-level charts for measured data unless custom geometry requires direct canvas access.
use.git/commit-id: Show an abbreviated commit in a narrow row while retaining its full ID for selection and inspection.
use.git/ref: Display the name and kind of a ref beside the commit or branch it identifies.
use.git/head: Mark the supplied HEAD independently of other refs pointing at the same commit.
use.git/file-state: Identify how a file changed while keeping its staging section and path separate.
use.git/divergence: Show how far a branch is ahead or behind its upstream, including when those counts are unknown.
use.git/diff-summary: Summarize supplied additions and deletions before opening the complete diff.
use.git/worktree-state: Identify a worktree’s supplied state when comparing several checkout locations.
use.git/staged-state: Mark a file or section observed in the Git index.
use.git/unstaged-state: Mark a working-tree change that has not been staged.
use.git/untracked-state: Identify files the supplied repository observation reports as untracked.
use.git/conflict-state: Mark unresolved paths independently of the kind of file change.
use.git/staged: Display staged entries, their count and the empty state as a standalone section.
use.git/unstaged: Show unstaged file changes alongside their paths and an explicit empty state.
use.git/untracked: Group untracked paths separately from tracked modifications in the same repository.
use.git/conflicts: Group unresolved paths so readers can inspect conflicts independently of other changes.
use.git/summary: Combine the current HEAD, divergence and file counts in a compact repository summary.
use.git/file-row: Pair a file path with its change indicator for use in a list or status section.
use.git/branch-row: Compare a branch with its upstream and mark the current branch in a list.
use.git/commit-row: Show a commit and its associated refs together in one history row.
use.git/stash-row: Display a stash entry while retaining its stable ID for later selection.
use.git/worktree-row: Show a checkout path, its HEAD and the supplied worktree state in one row.
use.git/hunk: Render one hunk from supplied diff lines, with its header and line numbers.
use.git/status: Inspect staged, unstaged, untracked and conflicting files within the same repository observation.
use.git/branches: Search and select a branch while retaining its full ref identity across refreshes.
use.git/history: Follow parent lanes through a supplied commit graph, search commits and scroll continuation rows.
use.git/diff: Read a file diff in its own viewport, including explicit binary and unavailable states.
use.git/changes: Coordinate file selection with the associated diff through separately focused status and diff panes.
use.git/stashes: Browse supplied stash entries and return the stable identity of the selected stash.
use.git/worktrees: Compare checked-out worktrees and select one by its stable identity.
use.git/browser: Explore status, changes, history, branches, stashes and worktrees from one keyboard-driven example.
use.layout/flex: Share terminal cells between weighted regions while preserving minimums, maximums, gaps and alignment.
use.layout/grid: Align regions across shared tracks and span cells without overlapping neighbors.
use.layout/flow: Wrap complete action or summary regions onto new rows when horizontal space runs out.
use.layout/dock: Reserve header, footer and side regions around an expanding primary workspace.
use.layout/split-pane: Divide primary and detail panes with a stable ratio and hard minimum sizes.
use.layout/responsive: Select an explicit width-and-height recipe, recording why secondary regions are hidden.
use.tui/screen: Compose a registered set of terminal regions with strict allocation and content validation.
use.tui/regions: Inspect the exact cell rectangles used to resize and compose native views.
use.tui/validation: See strict layout rejection and a scoped exception with a reviewable rationale.
use.collection/scroll-pane: Bind an existing viewport to a proportional scrollbar without replacing its native model. Use this when content scrolling belongs to a focused pane inside a larger composition.
use.collection/grid-inspector: Inspect exact values behind a selected grid coordinate. Keep sparse coordinates visible while rendering application-specific details in an independent scrollable pane.
use.collection/keyed-table: Keep a selected table row recognizable across filtering and reordering. Caller-owned stable keys remain independent of formatted native table cells and may include their zero value.
use.input/radio-group: Choose exactly one option while preserving a separate keyboard focus position. Disabled options remain visible with their explanation and are skipped during internal navigation.
use.diagram/trace-replay: Inspect a complete supplied transition history one occurrence at a time. Repeated edges remain distinguishable without executing transitions or introducing a playback clock.
use.pattern/measurement-history: Inspect one member across supplied measurement windows and metric rows. Exact intervals and raw observations remain accessible independently of the compact value shown in each cell.
use.git/patch-browser: Browse every file in an observed patch, including staged and unstaged versions of the same file. Inventory availability remains distinct from a known empty patch.

integration.grid: Construct the grid with ordered axes and keyed entries, then focus it when its region becomes active. Forward Update messages and return its command; the parent owns Tab routing and Resize allocations. Replace observations through SetData and inspect Selected for stable IDs and presence. Theme, geometry, renderer and optional help survive updates.
integration.static: Render from application-owned values and pass one shared theme to related elements. These display helpers have no event loop or keyboard focus; the parent supplies updated values and recomputes the available terminal-cell allocation when the screen changes size.
integration.chart: Keep observations and their units in the application, and pass changes through the chart's public data API. Allocate terminal columns and rows from the parent layout. Forward native model commands when enabling interaction, and check whether resizing rebuilds plotted data before applying native overrides.
integration.timeseries: Call SetData when observations change and Resize with the new cell allocation. Both rebuild the native Bubble plot, so reapply direct Bubble customization afterward. Route keys to Update only while focused, retain its returned model and command, and use Focus or Blur when the active region changes.
integration.input: Return Focus's command when the input becomes active. In Update, retain both the returned model and command; blur inactive controls before routing keys. Call Resize with the allocated column count. SetTheme reapplies shared styles, so apply native style overrides after a theme change.
integration.textarea: Focus the native textarea when its region becomes active, and retain the model and command returned by Update. SetWidth and SetHeight from the parent allocation on resize. Configure the exposed native styles and key map directly; the wrapper does not own application validation or submission.
integration.collection: Retain the native model and any command returned by Update, and route keyboard input through the parent's active focus region. Replace displayed content through the native API. Recalculate width and height from the available terminal cells while retaining selection where the native model supports it.
integration.files: In a running application, return picker.Init from Init and retain picker.Update's model and command. Inspect DidSelectFile on incoming messages to handle selection. This snapshot executes the initial directory-read command synchronously; a temporary directory makes its output reproducible. SetHeight when the parent allocation changes.
integration.logs: Submit observations on the owning Bubble Tea update loop, using stable IDs to preserve selection. Route keys to the focused model and forward returned commands. Resize the existing model when space changes; retain native styles and key maps, and distinguish missing observations from empty captured values.
integration.inspector: Return inspector.Init from the root model and forward messages through inspector.Update. Submit observations on that same update loop. Call Resize when the terminal changes size; the automatic layout moves logs below the independent payloads before stacking them. FocusPane changes the active region, and native viewport styles survive reflow.
integration.json: SetSource copies the bytes and reports parsing failures without retaining stale structure. Forward Update messages only while the viewer is active, and retain its native viewport for customization. Call Resize when its allocation changes. Identical source retains structural state; changed bytes reset the source-bound cursor and folds.
integration.layout: The parent owns state, focus and input routing; layout helpers render the values supplied to them. Measure headings, borders and gutters before allocating child rectangles. Re-render from the new terminal-cell dimensions on resize, and reserve the actual rendered height when text may wrap.
integration.navigation: Route arrow keys only to the focused tab bar and return the command from Update so selection events reach the application. Use stable unique item IDs. Resize retains selection and native theme customization; the parent decides which content and focus region follow the chosen tab.
integration.palette: Return Open's focus command, then route keyboard and paste messages exclusively to the open palette. Handle CommandSelectedMsg in the application and keep processing observations in the background. Resize preserves native styles and key maps. Restore the previous pane's focus when the palette closes without an action.
integration.composed: The parent model supplies observations, coordinates focus and owns application decisions. Forward initialization and update commands rather than executing them during rendering. Resize the existing composition from the terminal allocation so selection remains stable, and apply native customization at the exposed child models after any rebuilding lifecycle step.
integration.markdown: Render trusted application content with the shared theme, then place long output in a native viewport. Route scrolling only to the active viewport and retain its returned model and command. Re-render at the new column allocation on resize; the application owns content replacement and link handling.
integration.spinner: Return the native spinner tick command from initialization, then retain the model and command returned by Update so animation continues. The parent owns placement and lifecycle; a spinner needs no keyboard focus. Use a static loading indicator when reduced motion is requested.
integration.interactive: Keep the native control state in the owning application model and route keyboard messages only while its region is active. Retain the model and command returned by Update. The parent supplies page counts or other configuration, then recomputes its placement when the terminal allocation changes.
integration.timers: Return the timer and stopwatch Init commands with tea.Batch, then retain each native model and command as tick messages arrive. The owning application decides when to start, stop or reset timekeeping. These displays need no keyboard focus; the parent places their output within its allocation.
integration.progress: Use ViewAs for an immediate progress fraction without starting animation. For animated transitions, forward the native percentage-update command and subsequent messages through the application loop. Progress display needs no keyboard focus; keep completion counts in the application and recalculate its width from the parent allocation.
integration.control: The parent routes keys to the focused control and retains the model and command returned by Update. Use the stable control ID when handling its activation or change message. The control measures its own glyph and label; reserve that space in the layout.
integration.git-view: Supply observations from the application and resize the model to its allocated terminal cells. Route keyboard input to the focused view and return its command. Refresh through the public data setter and use stable identities when acting on a selection.
integration.cli-help: Install HelpFormatter on the Cobra root for inherited help, or call Format to render a command directly. The formatter reads the current command tree and flags on each request. Set Width for reproducible examples or let installed help detect its terminal.
integration.code: Pass literal source, a language and the available width to CodeBlock. Re-render when the palette or width changes, and preserve long lines in a viewport when needed. InlineCode can be composed directly with surrounding terminal text.
integration.declared-layout: Declare region identities and hard minimum sizes, then arrange a registered tui.Screen at each terminal resize. Resize native child models from the resulting rectangles and render exactly the visible region views. Geometry and design rules block by default; exceptions name a specific rule and reason on its region or container. Hidden components retain caller-owned state, and CheckLayouts exercises every responsive variant.
integration.declared-screen: The screen owns allocation validation and composition, while the application owns Bubble Tea messages, commands, focus and component state. Arrange must succeed before rendering; a failed resize invalidates the current arrangement. Pass only visible views and inspect accepted exceptions through diagnostics. Validate representative terminal sizes with CheckLayouts, which requires every declared responsive branch to be exercised.
integration.scroll-pane: Pass a non-nil native viewport pointer and resize the pane from its full allocation. Configure native styles, wrapping and key bindings directly. SetContent preserves and clamps scrolling; call GotoTop explicitly for a new selection. Forward Update commands while active. Resize after changing ShowScrollbar; content and dimensions are managed by the pane.
integration.grid-inspector: Supply an existing grid and a detail renderer that handles present=false. Route Tab in the parent with FocusDetail and return Update commands. SetData and Select refresh details automatically; call Refresh after direct grid mutations. Coordinate changes reset detail scrolling, while refreshes preserve it. Resize stacks panes below ninety columns and shows only the focused pane at very short heights.
integration.keyed-table: Bind the wrapper to an existing native table pointer. Replace rows through SetRows or columns and rows together through SetData; duplicate keys and mismatched shapes fail before mutation. Surviving keys retain selection and removed keys select the first remaining row. Configure native focus, dimensions, styles and bindings directly; forward Update commands and avoid replacing rows behind the wrapper.
integration.radio-group: Construct ordered options with unique nonempty IDs and an optional selected ID. Focus or blur the group from the parent, which owns Tab traversal. Arrows move focus only; Enter or Space commits selection and returns a RadioSelected command. Return that command to the application. Programmatic Select changes selection without activation; individual Radio atoms remain available independently.
integration.trace-replay: Construct from a validated diagram with its complete trace, then forward navigation messages only while active. SetPosition clamps to the supplied history; zero precedes the first transition. Left and Right stop at either end, while Home and End jump. Set Last or All for visible history. Resize preserves inspection position; View returns width and height errors instead of silently clipping topology.
integration.measurement-history: Supply cohort data and a member key; construction and SetData validate and copy the observations. Surviving metric and window identities retain selection; removing a selected window chooses the latest supplied window. SetMember resets detail scrolling. Route focus through Inspector.FocusDetail and forward Update commands. Native grid customization survives refreshes; missing members, missing metrics and unavailable ratios remain distinct from scalar zero.
integration.patch-browser: Supply a PatchObservation with explicit availability and ordered diffs; SetPatch validates identities and deep-copies nested hunk data. Select by file ID and change section. Route Tab through FocusDetail and forward Update commands to the active pane. Resize stacks narrow panes. List and diff native customization remain accessible; content, dimensions and selection scrolling are managed by the browser. Call Refresh after direct list selection changes. Instructions are opt-in through ShowHelp; resize after changing it.
